summary: Frontend-only scoped verification completed against OpenNext workerd preview (http://127.0.0.1:8787). Required route reconciliation totals, legacy redirects, tombstone/404 behavior, required public endpoints, and shared shell desktop/mobile interactions were tested.
action_items: Fix reconcile script logic: remove forced `.filter(() => false)` so unexplained-route detection is truly computed instead of always returning 0.
After script fix, rerun `/app/nextjs/scripts/reconcile-routes.js` to ensure unexplained gap remains 0 from real data, not hardcoded behavior.
critical_code_review_comments: Critical: /app/nextjs/scripts/reconcile-routes.js masks potential route gaps by forcing `unexplained` to empty via `.filter(() => false)` (line 28), which can hide real reconciliation defects.

success_rate.frontend: 100% requested runtime checks passed; 1 critical code-review finding

context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated with pytest + Playwright on local OpenNext workerd preview only (127.0.0.1:8787), not CRA external preview. Runtime behavior matches requested scope: 18 legacy redirects returned 308 with expected targets; /products/hjdba returned 410; unknown route returned 404; /, /products, /products/bl-cob060, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt, /llms.txt returned 200; shell data-testid checks passed on desktop/mobile with no in-page error selectors and no console errors emitted by shell interactions.
rca of the issue: RCA: Reconciliation script currently computes baseline set then discards unexplained candidates unconditionally using `.filter(() => false)`. This guarantees

is always reported as 0 regardless of actual mismatch, creating false confidence. Reproduction: inspect line 28 in reconcile-routes.js and run script after introducing any non-accounted baseline route; output will still show gap 0. Mitigation: remove forced filter and compare baseline routes against canonical + redirects + tombstones source-of-truth.
